params.body:
Builds on the design system of #925 (text roles, `x-ui.page-head`, `x-ui.filter-row`, `x-ui.segmented`).

## What this is

The insights tabs were named after where their data came from, so the same answer stood in three places and the question "is the trade moving" nowhere. This pull request adds two tabs that each answer one question, puts every insights tab and the garage's own page on one pattern, and gives every chart one palette.

No migration, no new table, no new route. The deploy runs nothing beyond the usual build. Two new read-only classes (`App\Support\Momentum`, `App\Support\GarageHealth`); the insights controller gains the two tabs and "Cijfers herberekenen" clears their cache as well.

Two things a user will notice outside the new tabs: Beheer > Inzichten now opens on Momentum (it is the first tab), and the period is called `periode` in every address (My insights used `window`; an old link with `?window=` falls back to the default period).

## Momentum: is the trade moving (rules P2-10.30 to P2-10.39)

One sentence on top (the trade speeds up, slows down or holds, from cars sold per day over the last 28 whole days against the 28 before; more than 10 percent either way is a direction), four figures under it, then the views that prove it on one time axis of whole weeks. One period (30 days, 90 days, 12 months; default 90) and one garage filter apply to everything.

| Term | Definition | Column |
|---|---|---|
| Car in | added to a garage's own stock | `vehicles.created_at` |
| Car out | sold | `vehicles.sold_at` |
| Left without a sale | deleted while unsold; drawn apart, never called a sale | `deleted_at` with `sold_at` empty |
| Standing | added, not sold, not deleted | |
| Time to sell | whole days from `created_at` to `sold_at`, as a rolling median over 28 days; no median under 10 sales | |

Left out on the car side: bidding cars (`for_export = 1`), drafts (`is_complete = 0`) and the copy a buy-over leaves at the buyer (`seller_vehicle_id`). A buy-over counts once, as a sale at the seller; the screen says how many sales went to a colleague. Deleted rows are read on purpose (`withTrashed`): the day a car was sold does not change because the sheet was cleaned up later. Who entered the car plays no role here: a car is a car, also when platform staff typed it in.

Bidding momentum, per week because the channel sees a handful of offers a week: offers started (`export_vehicles.created_at`, the first start, not a restart), bids placed (`export_bids.created_at`, withdrawn bids included), how many garages and traders bid, and what became of the offers that ended: the share with a bid and the share with a winner, the latter only over offers older than the 15 days in which a winner can still be chosen.

## Garages: who is active, who is slipping (rules P2-10.40 to P2-10.45)

Every account with one status and a sentence that says why. No score.

An act is something the garage itself did, from traces that reach back over the whole history: a car added, a car sold (not to a colleague: that is the buyer's act), a car bought over, an offer, an order form, a car offered for bidding, a bid, a Car-Pass or chassis lookup. A lead does not count (the customer writes it). Signing in and opening screens do not decide the status, because they are only kept since 19 and 25 September 2026; they stand beside it as a second signal.

Status, in this order:

1. **closed**: both modules off, whatever it did
2. **never started**: no act at all
3. **new**: first act at most 30 days old
4. **silent**: no act in the last 28 whole days; **gone** when the last act is more than 365 days back
5. **growing** or **slowing**: the last 28 days differ from the 28 before by at least 3 acts and by a factor 1.5 (one act becoming two is not growth)
6. **stable**: everything else

Active is new, growing, stable or slowing. Closed accounts stand behind their own count and never count as active. Acts by platform staff, under their own account or inside a garage's account, are left out wherever the row says who did it (cars added, offers, order forms, lookups, sign-ins); offers and order forms also take the existing demo filter. The list opens on who to call first (silent and slowing, largest drop first), a row shows twelve weeks as a small chart, an opened garage shows 26 weeks per kind of act, and a chart per month says: this month = last month + new + back - stopped.

## One pattern on every tab and on the garage's page (rule P2-10.46)

Momentum, Garages, Klanten en omzet, Gebruik, Werking, Kaart and My insights now stand on the same pieces: the page head with its actions as text, one filter line under the tabs (the period as a segmented choice, called `periode` everywhere), the answer on its own surface as one sentence with at most five figures, then blocks with the question as title, the answer, the proof and one quiet note; long definitions and sources sit behind "Hoe dit geteld wordt". Text takes roles only: `insights.css` sets no size of its own.

What that changed per tab, in short: Klanten en omzet lost its six tiles and its window choice halfway down the page (the window is the filter line, the answer is the sales value with four figures); Gebruik lost its own "Periode" card and opens with a verdict; Werking is one card with a row per subject instead of eight loose cards; Kaart has its controls in the filter line and its sources behind the fold; My insights has questions as titles, no icons, nothing coloured in an answer.

Enforced by `EveryInsightsTabStandsOnOnePatternTest`; `InsightsKeepTheirRulesTest` follows the new pattern and rule P2-13.9 says it.

## One chart palette

Six tokens in `resources/css/colour.css`, read by the Blade charts through the stylesheet and by the scripts through `getComputedStyle`. No colour in a view or a script any more (tested).

| Token | Value | Means |
|---|---|---|
| `--ui-data-1` | `#5f93cc` | what is counted: in, acts, bids, dealers, the meters |
| `--ui-data-2` | `#0a836c` | the counterpart in a chart of two: sold, traders |
| `--ui-data-context` | `#bcc0c7` | context: left without a sale, stayed, unknown |
| `--ui-data-bad` | `#b5544d` | only what is wrong: stopped, never started, without a bid |
| `--ui-data-1-step-1..3` | `#e3ecf7` `#c5d7ee` `#9dbbe0` | the blue lighter: hour grid, weekend and running bar |
| `--ui-data-1-deep` | `#3f6fa9` | small marks only: a top-5 line, the bands over 90 days in a meter |

Against white the blue reaches 3.2:1 and the green 4.7:1; the two stay apart under colour blindness and in grey. The running period is hatched. Where two series inside the family could not be told apart they differ in shape (a dashed line, a ring).

## Performance

- Momentum: cached for an hour per day, period and garage. Every query is bounded by the period plus what the comparison a quarter ago needs (at most about 14 months back); the one unbounded read is what stands today, which is the stock itself. `vehicles` has no index on `created_at`, `sold_at` or `deleted_at`, so each query reads the table once.
- Found and fixed while checking: the sales query asked per sale whether a buy-over copy exists, in the select list, and `seller_vehicle_id` has no index: the whole table once per sale. The set is now read once and looked up in memory.
- Garages: one computation for all accounts, cached for an hour per day. The first and last act per garage read each of the eight sources over the whole history (by design: "never started" and "gone" need it), the per-day counts only the last 13 months.
- "Cijfers herberekenen" leaves all of it behind at once.

## Where the data is weak

- `sold_at` is the moment of the click, not of the sale. A garage that marks ten cars as sold on a Friday gives a spike in the day bars; the 28-day average absorbs it.
- Undoing a sale (partner API only) empties `sold_at`: the sale disappears from history.
- `created_at` is the day of insertion, also for a feed. A garage that joins and imports 80 cars gives 80 "in" on one day, and all of them start at zero days standing. The screen does not split feeds off yet (`created_via = 'api'` marks them).
- A car sold on the day it was entered (entered only to write an order form) pulls the median down. They count.
- `for_export` and `is_complete` are today's state: an own car later offered for bidding leaves the car side retroactively.
- Only sold cars have a time to sell; the age of what stands is shown next to it for that reason.
- Shared stocklist against own stock only cannot be split for a sold car.
- There is no flag any more to leave demo garages out. Cars of an account that was closed and never sold or deleted them still count as standing in Momentum.
- On bids and bidding offers the row keeps only the garage, so staff cannot be left out there; the same holds for a sale and a buy-over.
- Sign-ins exist since 19 September 2026 and signed-in days since 25 September 2026.

## Open questions for the owner

1. The verdict of a tab is in `lead` (18) and not in `headline` (22), so the figures (26) stay the only large text. Keep?
2. The green is the darkest series now, so it differs from the blue in grey as well. Keep, or lighter and differing in hue only?
3. Gebruik, Werking and Garages have a verdict without large figures, because the list under it says the numbers. Keep?
4. The page head has "Cijfers herberekenen" while Gebruik and Werking keep their own "Nu verversen" for another cache. One button for all?
5. Is "statijd" the word a Flemish dealer uses, or "stockdagen"?
6. Should Momentum leave out the standing cars of closed accounts?
7. Next step, not in here: split Klanten en omzet (six blocks to a tab Omzet, the rest replaced by Momentum and Garages), move views per channel to a tab Bereik, make Kaart a view inside Garages. Tab names follow that split and are unchanged for now.

## What to look at on production after the deploy

The demo has 23 cars and a dozen garages; real counts differ.

- Momentum, first load per period (30 days, 90 days, 12 months) and with one large garage chosen: does it answer in well under a second uncached? If not, an index on `vehicles (sold_at)` and `(created_at)` is the fix.
- Garages, first load: the same question; it reads eight sources over the whole history.
- Momentum, "in": look for one-day spikes from feed imports, and whether "left without a sale" is large enough to need an explanation.
- Momentum, stock: compare the number standing with the stock block on Klanten en omzet; Momentum is wider (it does not ask `on_stock`), and closed accounts may inflate it.
- Time to sell: how many sales have zero days, and whether the median is believable for a garage you know.
- Garages: the counts per status against what you know (how many closed, never started, gone), and three garages you know well: does the sentence fit?
- Bidding: the share with a winner over offers older than 15 days.
- Every tab at 390 wide once, with real names and amounts: the garage rows, the measure list of Gebruik and the rows of Werking.

## Checked

Full PHPUnit suite, PHPStan, eslint, vitest and pint on the added files, locally on the main this builds on. Texts exist in nl, fr, en and de with the same keys. Rules P2-10.30 to P2-10.46 are in `docs/bedrijfsregels/32-p2-mijn-garage.md` as draft rules, each with its `@rule` tag in a test.
params.title: Insights: Momentum and Garages, every tab on one pattern, one chart palette
